PullRequest.Title: Markdown editor: render Mermaid blocks like the Markdown preview
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/344300

In the experimental Markdown editor, Mermaid diagrams looked different from the same diagram in the Markdown preview. They used Mermaid's default purple theme, which is hard to read in dark themes (also reported in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/330433). Small diagrams were stretched to the full column width, and `markdown-mermaid.maxHeight` was ignored. The editor had its own Mermaid renderer in `markdown-language-features`, separate from the preview's in `mermaid-markdown-features`.

This PR moves the editor's Mermaid code block editor into `mermaid-markdown-features`. It is contributed through `markdown.codeBlockEditorProviders` (export API), so editor and preview share one renderer, theme mapping, and set of settings.

Demo, recorded in Code OSS from this branch. Markdown editor on the left, Markdown preview on the right:
- light, dark, and high-contrast themes
- a live edit
- `markdown-mermaid.maxHeight: "300px"` capping the initial height
- dragging the height grip past the cap

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5ba9589a-0932-4ba2-a331-16e01789f621

## What changes for users

- **Theme:** diagrams use the preview's VS Code theme mapping and render again when the color theme changes.
- **Size:** diagrams render at their natural size, at most the column width and centered, like in the preview. The embedded editor's frame follows that height (`reportSize`) without scrollbars.
- **`markdown-mermaid.maxHeight`:**
  - It still defaults to empty, meaning no cap, in both the preview and the editor.
  - When set to a pixel value, the editor uses it as `maxAutomaticHeight`: it caps the initial height, and users can still drag the grip beyond it.
  - Other CSS lengths, such as `80vh`, still apply in the preview but leave the editor uncapped.
- **`markdown-mermaid.resizable`:** controls the editor's height grip.
- Setting changes apply to open Markdown editors right away.

## Changes

**mermaid-markdown-features**
- New `MermaidCodeBlockEditorProvider` (`src/markdownEditor/`). It resolves the editor page with the current `markdown-mermaid` settings, which are injected the same way as in the preview. It returns `presentation: { resizable, fullWidth, fullView, maxAutomaticHeight }` and fires `onDidChange` when settings change.
- New guest `preview-src/markdownEditor/index.ts`, built to `markdown-editor-out/`. It connects via `WebEditorClient` and reuses the preview's `loadExtensionConfig`, `VsCodeMermaidThemeTracker`, and render helpers.
  - The Markdown editor injects the theme as CSS variables plus `color-scheme`, without VS Code's body classes. The guest derives `vscode-dark`/`vscode-light` from `color-scheme` and re-renders when the injected theme changes.
  - It reports the height the diagram has at the frame's full width. Measuring the rendered height instead let a scrollbar narrow the diagram and then keep itself.
- New dependency `@vscode/web-editors`.
- `scripts/markdownEditor.browser.test.mts` replaces the old Mermaid browser test. It hosts the guest with a real `WebEditorHost` and checks rendering, natural size, theme switching, live edits, and error recovery.

**markdown-language-features**
- Export-API code block editor providers can expose an optional `onDidChange` event. When it fires, open Markdown editors resolve that provider's blocks again.
- `maxAutomaticHeight` is accepted in the code block editor presentation (contribution schema, descriptor validation, merge).
- The Markdown editor document now uses the theme's `color-scheme`. Before, embedded frames had `color-scheme: dark` in dark themes while the editor document was `normal`, so Chromium painted an opaque backdrop behind every embedded editor. That showed as a dark box behind Mermaid diagrams and other embedded editors.
- Removed the built-in Mermaid renderer (`markdown-editor-src/mermaid/`), its build plugin and test, and the `mermaid` dependency.
- Updated `@vscode/markdown-editor` from 0.0.2-136 to 0.0.2-147. This brings the embedded editor chrome from https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-packages/pull/392 (hover outline, toolbar, snapping grips, `maxAutomaticHeight`) and the presentation protocol from https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-packages/pull/396.

## Validation

- `npm run test-extension -- -l markdown-language-features`: 192 passing. This includes new tests for `maxAutomaticHeight` validation and presentation merging.
- `node --test scripts/markdownEditor.browser.test.mts` in `mermaid-markdown-features` passes.
- Typecheck of both extensions (including `tsconfig.markdownEditor.json` and `preview-src`), ESLint, hygiene, and `check-markdown-editor-package-json` all pass.
- Manual check in Code OSS with the published 0.0.2-147 package, comparing the editor and preview side by side:
  - Light Modern, Dark Modern, and Default High Contrast.
  - Live theme switching.
  - Setting `maxHeight` while the editor is open.
  - Resizing past the cap.
  - Frame heights equal the diagram heights, with no stray scrollbars.

Pan and zoom in the editor, as toolbar actions, are a later step.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The eager call, its position before host connection, the static addon imports, the old guest comparison, and per-block iframe lifecycle are all directly visible in repository code/tests. Exact milliseconds and tree-shaken bundle size are uncertain, which limits severity, but not the mechanism or scaling.
Findings.PerformanceResource: JavaScript module loading, parsing/evaluation CPU, and per-iframe addon/module objects
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The cost is paid once for every instantiated Mermaid code-block iframe; documents with multiple Mermaid blocks create multiple isolated iframe realms, so parse/evaluation and retained module state grow with the number of active or parked frames even though extension-resource bytes may be browser-cached.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased time to first diagram render and higher CPU/memory usage when opening or scrolling Markdown documents containing Mermaid blocks.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The removed built-in guest imported only `mermaid`, connected to the host, initialized Mermaid, and rendered the block. It did not import or register the optional ELK, tidy-tree, or ZenUML packages.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new guest statically imports the shared module, whose top-level imports include `@mermaid-js/layout-elk`, `@mermaid-js/layout-tidy-tree`, and `@mermaid-js/mermaid-zenuml`, then awaits `registerMermaidAddons()` before `WebEditorClient.connect`. Thus even a basic flowchart cannot render until every iframe has loaded and initialized optional diagram support.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added RIGHT line 28 places unconditional optional-addon registration on the startup critical path of each new Mermaid iframe; the deleted guest's startup path had no corresponding registration or addon imports.
Findings.Title: Lazy-load optional Mermaid add-ons
Findings.Impact: Opening an experimental Markdown editor with ordinary Mermaid flowcharts now performs optional-addon startup in each diagram iframe. The iframe factory uses one isolated frame per rendered block and parks frames for reuse, so several blocks multiply and retain this work; users see slower initial rendering and more renderer-process memory.
Findings.Evidence: `index.ts` calls `await registerMermaidAddons()` before line 29 connects to the host. `preview-src/shared/index.ts` statically imports ELK, tidy-tree, and ZenUML and the helper registers all three; the lockfile shows ELK depends on `elkjs`/d3 and ZenUML pulls `@zenuml/core` and its renderer/parser dependency graph. The existing browser fixture for the same `VirtualizedIframeEmbeddedEditorFactory` demonstrates two matching blocks create two iframes and that removed blocks leave those frames parked until disposal. The deleted `mermaidGuest.ts` used only `mermaid` and had no addon registration.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep basic Mermaid startup limited to the core renderer. Split the editor entry/shared module so optional layout and external-diagram packages are dynamically imported and registered only when the block's syntax/config actually selects them (while preserving one registration per iframe), then connect and render ordinary diagrams without awaiting those packages.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or scroll the experimental Markdown editor to ordinary Mermaid flowcharts
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The Markdown editor loads the export-API provider, resolves one descriptor for the document/language, creates a nested iframe for each instantiated block, loads the local guest module, awaits optional-addon registration, connects the WebEditorClient, then parses/renders and reports size. The unconditional addon initialization is on the critical path and is the reported regression.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the export-API descriptor across the extension-host/webview RPC path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One effective resolution per provider/document/language while the descriptor cache is warm, not per Mermaid block.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The built-in Mermaid provider supplied its descriptor inside the editor webview and did not activate/resolve through an extension export API.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before matching blocks can receive the iframe descriptor; coalesced and not itself the finding.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load extension-local iframe HTML/module resources through the webview resource loader; the module bundle includes statically imported optional Mermaid addons.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: HTML/module fetches occur per iframe navigation, with likely browser-cache hits after the first; JavaScript parse/evaluation and registration still occur per iframe realm.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The removed guest used a self-contained HTML bundle importing only Mermaid core, without ELK, tidy-tree, or ZenUML registration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Guest module loading and addon registration must complete before host connection and first render.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of Mermaid blocks instantiated by the virtualized editor. Each rendered block has an isolated iframe; the existing factory fixture establishes one frame per matching block and parks frames for reuse.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Descriptors are coalesced by provider/document/language, but matching block iframes initialize independently and can start concurrently; there is no shared limiter across frames. Resource HTTP caching can coalesce bytes, not per-realm module evaluation or addon registration.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The resolved descriptor is cached per contribution/document/language. Local script bytes may be warm in Chromium's cache, and parked iframes are reused, but each newly created iframe has a separate module realm and retains its initialized addon state until factory disposal. There is no negative-cache issue on the successful path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: added line 28, shared static imports, lockfile dependencies, old guest, and per-block iframe behavior directly establish the eager per-frame cost.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact output-chunk sizes, Chromium code-cache reuse, and typical Mermaid-block counts are not measured. The optional packages' dependency graph and per-frame execution are concrete, so uncertainty lowers severity rather than mechanism confidence.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity eager-work regression: optional diagram engines are placed on every basic diagram's startup path and retained per iframe.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each content notification invokes render, aborts the prior controller, initializes Mermaid configuration, parses/renders into a detached staging node, swaps the result, measures layout, and reports size to the host. There are no filesystem, subprocess, database, or external-network calls on this path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Receive updated block text and report the resulting height through WebEditorClient.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One content notification and at most one deduplicated height report per accepted render.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The removed guest used the same WebEditorClient content-change and report-size boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Content delivery starts rendering; the size report follows rendering and controls frame layout.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Edit-event frequency and Mermaid source/diagram complexity for the affected block; separate visible blocks have separate clients.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each iframe handles its own events. Abort marks superseded renders, but Mermaid parse/render work is only checked after awaited operations, so rapid edits may overlap; the deleted guest also launched uncancelled render work per content update, so the diff does not establish a separate high-confidence regression beyond the eager addon startup.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No render-result cache. The iframe and initialized modules are reused for edits; superseded DOM results are discarded.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the call path and overlap behavior; insufficiently high for a distinct diff-caused performance impact beyond the reported addon initialization.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The shared helper explicitly parses before rendering, but repository evidence does not establish Mermaid's internal parse reuse or enough measured incremental cost for a second finding.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: rapid-update work largely existed in the deleted guest, and the incremental parse cost is not sufficiently quantified/proven here.

Scenarios.Scenario: Switch the VS Code color theme with Mermaid blocks open
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Theme CSS injected into each frame mutates its head, the MutationObserver updates light/dark classes, resolves theme variables, and rerenders only when the fingerprint changes. Rendering and layout reporting complete before each diagram visually settles.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: extensions/markdown-language-features/markdown-editor-src/codeBlockEditorTheme.ts transitively consumed by the new guest
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Propagate workbench theme CSS into nested editor frames.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One theme propagation per live frame for a workbench theme change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Theme CSS propagation already existed for embedded editors, but the removed Mermaid guest did not rerender its diagram from that signal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Starts per-frame theme recomputation and required rerender; no filesystem or external network access.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of live/parked Mermaid iframe realms and diagram complexity.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each iframe observes and rerenders independently; theme changes can fan out concurrently across open blocks, with no global limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Theme variables are fingerprint-cached inside each tracker. Equal fingerprints suppress rendering; rendered SVGs are not cached across themes or frames.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that the new observer rerenders each changed frame; the work is required by the PR's user-visible theme feature.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Theme switches are infrequent and realistic simultaneous frame counts vary.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: this is an intentional, fingerprint-deduplicated cost of making open diagrams follow theme changes, and the trigger is infrequent.

Scenarios.Scenario: Change a markdown-mermaid setting while editors are open
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The extension configuration listener fires provider onDidChange; MarkdownEditorProvider clears resolved descriptor caches, reloads provider definitions, posts them to every open editor, resolves the provider again per document/language, and refreshes matching embedded editors. A changed HTML hash changes runtimeKey so old-setting frames are not reused.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Post refreshed provider definitions and resolve updated descriptors between extension host and each editor webview.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At least one refresh per open editor panel; one effective descriptor resolve per panel/document/language, followed by matching block updates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The built-in editor Mermaid guest did not react to markdown-mermaid settings changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for open editors to adopt changed settings; the fan-out occurs only on explicit setting changes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of open Markdown editor panels containing matching Mermaid blocks and number of instantiated block frames.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All open panel listeners respond independently with no global limiter. Within a panel, resolution is coalesced per document/language, while iframe recreation/rendering can fan out per block.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Descriptor caches are deliberately invalidated. The provider API object/listener remains cached; the generated HTML/runtimeKey identifies one setting snapshot. Browser resource bytes remain warm, but new frame realms reinitialize modules.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for invalidation and panel fan-out, but low concern because setting changes are user-driven and infrequent.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical number of simultaneously open rich Markdown editors and blocks is unknown.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the refresh is necessary for the new live-setting behavior and is coalesced at descriptor resolution granularity.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resize a Mermaid editor frame or its containing column
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ResizeObserver invokes reportSize, computes aspect-ratio height using existing SVG metadata or a fallback geometry read, deduplicates equal heights, and sends a size report; the host then updates frame height.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Report a changed content height from guest to host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one report per distinct computed height per frame; ResizeObserver callbacks with unchanged height are suppressed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The deleted guest also observed its container, computed aspect-ratio height, deduplicated, and called client.reportSize.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Needed to settle iframe layout without scrollbars; it follows rendering or width changes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Resize event frequency times number of visible Mermaid frames.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Browser ResizeObserver batches notifications; each frame independently deduplicates unchanged heights.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The last reported numeric height suppresses duplicate IPC. No persistent collection grows, and observers are disconnected on pagehide.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the observer, dedupe, and disposal are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Resize frequency depends on user interaction and workbench layout.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the diff preserves deduplicated sizing behavior and cleanup.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 26 changed files and traced editor opening, live edits, theme/config invalidation, iframe lifecycle, and size reporting. Submitted one medium eager-work finding for unconditional optional Mermaid addon initialization in every embedded frame; no regression-fix learning signal was warranted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
